subject.title: Manage Claw cron jobs through the gateway

question: Should agent-owned cron teardown become part of canonical `agents delete`, with Claw removal layering only Claw-specific provenance cleanup around that shared lifecycle?
rationale: The branch deliberately keeps ordinary agent deletion unchanged, while the scheduler ownership it creates is pinned to the agent; selecting the permanent deletion owner changes a public lifecycle boundary and cannot be resolved safely by an automated repair alone.

options.title: Centralize teardown in agent deletion
options.body: Make canonical agent deletion disable or preserve durable retry state for agent-owned cron jobs before committing agent removal, then keep Claw removal as a thin provenance-aware caller.

options.title: Keep Claw-only ownership
options.body: Retain cron teardown solely in `claws remove`, explicitly accept that ordinary agent deletion may leave experimental Claw cron ownership behind, and document the recovery path.

options.title: Defer the scheduler slice
options.body: Pause this stacked PR until maintainers settle the canonical ownership contract in the RFC or a narrower lifecycle change.

recommendation.title: Centralize teardown in agent deletion
recommendation.body: Make canonical agent deletion disable or preserve durable retry state for agent-owned cron jobs before committing agent removal, then keep Claw removal as a thin provenance-aware caller.
